question: When are no-passing-zone markings required at horizontal or vertical curves, and what should be done when successive no-passing zones are separated by less than 400 feet?
model_answer: Direct Answer: On two-way, two-lane or three-lane roadways with center line markings, no-passing zones must be established at horizontal and vertical curves where an engineering study shows passing must be prohibited, and no-passing zone markings must be used where the passing sight distance falls below the minimum in Table 3B-1 for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit. However, the evidence provided contains no provision addressing successive no-passing zones separated by less than 400 feet, so that part of the question cannot be answered from this evidence. Standards (mandatory): - "On two-way, two-lane or three-lane roadways where center line markings are installed, no-passing zones shall be established at vertical and horizontal curves and other locations where an engineering study indicates that passing must be prohibited because of inadequate sight distances or other special conditions." - "On roadways with center line markings, no-passing zone markings shall be used at horizontal or vertical curves where the passing sight distance is less than the minimum shown in Table 3B-1 for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit." - "No-passing zones shall be marked by either the one-direction no-passing zone pavement markings or the two-direction no-passing zone pavement markings described in Section 3B.01 and shown in Figures 3B-1 and 3B-3." - "No-passing zone markings shall be used on: A. Two-way roadways at lane-reduction transitions (see Section 3B.12), B. Approaches to obstructions that must be passed on the right (see Section 3B.13), C. Approaches to grade crossings (see Section 8C.02), and D. Approaches to crosswalks." - "When used, the NO PASSING ZONE sign shall be installed on the left-hand side of the roadway at the beginning of no-passing zones identified by pavement markings or DO NOT PASS signs or both." Citations: - Section 3B.03 Standard §3 (p.543) - Section 3B.03 Standard §4 (p.543) - Section 3B.03 Standard §1 (p.542) - Section 3B.03 Standard §2 (p.542) - Section 2C.53 Standard §1 (p.191) Note on the 400-foot question: The evidence supplied does not include any provision concerning successive no-passing zones separated by less than 400 feet. The evidence is insufficient to answer that portion of the question.
gold_answer: They are required on roadways with center line markings where passing sight distance is below the minimum in Table 3B-1 for the relevant speed. If successive no-passing zones are less than 400 feet apart, the markings should connect the zones.
